title: Trump: Jared Kushner purchases 666 5th Avenue, mob hangout
description_short: Trump: Jared Kushner purchases 666 5th Avenue, mob hangout
description_long: Jared Kushner bought the 41-story office tower at 666 Fifth Avenue in January 2007 for $1.8 billion, according to the linked New York Times headline. The supplied account says the purchase burdened his company with debt and that Qatar later helped pay it down. The original purchase predated Donald Trump’s presidency, while Kushner later served as a senior White House adviser. The TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202 and the Times article returned HTTP 403 in this review, so the financing terms, counterparties, and basis for calling the property a “mob hangout” could not be examined. The available material does not establish that the Qatar financing was coerced or that the building was controlled by a mob. Those claims require documentary support before they can be stated as fact.

description_short: Trump: News leaks that former Trump Campaign manager is writing a tell-all book

title: Trump: White House prepares Alex Jones to lead Capitol march on January 6
description_short: Trump: White House prepares Alex Jones to lead Capitol march on January 6
description_long: In the days before January 6, 2021, Alex Jones said someone from the White House had asked him to lead a march to the Capitol and that Roger Stone had originally been considered for the role. CNN reported that Jones helped jumpstart organization of the “Stop the Steal” rally, citing the grassroots organizer who filed the permits; it also relayed Wall Street Journal reporting about rally fundraising. CNN’s article supports Jones’s role in rally organizing, but it does not identify the alleged White House caller or independently confirm that officials asked him to lead the march. The claim about the request remains Jones’s account. Identifying the caller, the expected role, and any official communications would be necessary to establish the extent of White House involvement.

title: Trump says he is close to an Iran deal and reopening Strait of Hormuz, but Iran disagrees
description_short: Trump says he is close to an Iran deal and reopening Strait of Hormuz, but Iran disagrees
description_long: In late May 2026, Donald Trump said a deal with Iran was close and would end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran disputed his characterization. CBS reported that the Strait remained a sticking point amid dueling blockades, while Iran’s nuclear program and its stockpile of highly enriched uranium were Trump’s stated red lines. Pakistani army chief Asim Munir had been mediating, and Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian met him in Tehran. The ceasefire was holding, but Trump had given Tehran a loose deadline to return with an offer and had received options for resuming military action. The CBS report describes the issues and mediation but does not give the proposed agreement’s provisions or Iran’s specific objections. The AP link returned HTTP 403; the status and terms of mediation therefore remain only partly documented.
